method: Reads the top-level on: block of a workflow file and evaluates it for one event. The block is accepted as a single event name, a flow list (on: [push, pull_request]), or a map of event names to filter blocks; only push and pull_request are evaluated, and the other events are listed but not modelled. Inside an event, branches, branches-ignore, tags, tags-ignore, paths and paths-ignore take a block list, a flow list, or one inline value; types, cron, inputs and any other key are reported as not evaluated. Comments, quoted scalars and blank lines are tolerated, while tabs in indentation, inline mappings, block scalars, YAML anchors and aliases are refused rather than guessed: an unquoted pattern that starts with * is a YAML alias, so it has to be quoted. Patterns are matched against the whole branch name, tag name or repository-relative path, case-sensitively. * matches any run of characters except /, ** matches any run including /, ? matches zero or one of the character before it, + matches one or more of the character before it, [...] matches one character from a set or range, and a backslash escapes the next character; a pattern is matched from the start of the path, so */README.md does not match docs/README.md but **/README.md does. Patterns are checked in order and the last matching one decides, so a later pattern prefixed with ! removes a name that an earlier pattern included, and a positive pattern after a negative one adds it back; a ! pattern needs at least one positive pattern beside it. branches with branches-ignore, tags with tags-ignore and paths with paths-ignore cannot be combined in one event, because GitHub rejects the workflow, and the page refuses them instead of picking one. For push, a ref is filtered by the branches family when it is a branch and by the tags family when it is a tag, so defining only one family means the other kind of ref never triggers the workflow; with neither family every ref does. For pull_request the base branch is matched against the branches family. Path filters run on the changed paths and are satisfied when at least one path is included, or, for paths-ignore, when at least one path is not ignored; they are not evaluated at all for tag pushes. When a branches family and a paths family are both present, both have to be satisfied. Each filter row reports its outcome, the decisive pattern and its line, and each changed path reports the pattern that included or ignored it. Activity types, schedule cron, workflow_dispatch inputs, workflow_call, merge queues, reusable workflows, protected-branch rules and the branch-protection requirement for code-owner review are outside the model, and the page stores nothing and makes no requests.
